- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior trend.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model exhibits oscillation bias; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 5-day EWMA or using sentiment-weighted average.
- If sentiment is rising (increasing from 0.4 to 0.8+), model often fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment is trending up.
